source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 10a, 15-21; Instruction 13 Line 10a condition a (PDF page 15); Instruction 10 (PDF page 13); Schedule I (PDF page 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 10,550.00 + private employer pension (you) 40,000.00 = 50,550.00. Federal taxable income = 50,550.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 34,800.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 50,550.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 50,550.00. Worksheet 13A: You (age 64): not 65 or over on December 31, 2025 (and not disabled), so no exclusion on the qualifying 40,000.00. Line 10a = 0.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 0.00 (not a joint return). Line 15 total subtractions = Line 10a 0.00 = 0.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 50,550.00 - 0.00 = 50,550.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 3,350.00. Line 18 net income = 50,550.00 - 3,350.00 = 47,200.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 50,550.00 (not over 100,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 1 (Box A) = 3,200.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 47,200.00 - 3,200.00 = 44,000.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule I as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 41,000.00 = 1,947.50; total 2,037.50. (The tax table row 44,000-44,050, PDF page 36, gives 2,039; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 2,037.50. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). Whose age counts: 64 on December 31, 2025, so neither the pension exclusion (65 or over on the last day of the tax year, Line 10a) nor the 1,000 age exemption applies; not disabled (the disabled branch is not modelled).
